images.caption: Figure 1:Challenges inOut-of-Sight Causal Evolution. The camera first observes a subject (a vendor and his handcart), moves away to reveal a newly requested event (a collapsing building facade), and then moves back to the original scene. Previous methods (rows 1–4) exhibit various failures. In contrast, EvoWorld (row 5) realizes the event, revisits the original subject, and renders a causally plausible reaction while preserving subject and scene consistency.

Figure 2:Overview of the data engine for EvoWorld. Structured scenarios are rendered into single-take out-of-sight interactions, verified against visual evidence, temporally annotated, and converted into a training supervision dataset and evaluation benchmark.

Figure 3:Examples and statistics of EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench. The upper part illustrates representative training and benchmark examples, while the lower part summarizes their scale and scenario diversity.

Figure 4:Overview of the EvoWorld framework. (a) Stage 1 learns out-of-sight reactive rendering. (b) Stage 2 refines the renderer through online autoregressive adaptation. (c) Inference uses brain–renderer collaboration forOut-of-Sight Causal Evolution.
